findings.reason: §8's own discipline is "one owner" for edge, route count and claim state, and this names a shared mechanism (path→section, target∈section) with two pre-existing owners and a third arriving, so the author can fold the derivation into the owner `read_candidates` instead of adding a parallel one.
findings.text: the "section is the IDS top-level ancestor (first two path segments)" rule is already computed in at least two places and the "is this target inside the section" test in a third, and §8 introduces the section as the unit of its map-stage guard and of the new target-type rule without naming any of them as the owner to extend. Census of the type: `imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py:608` (`WITH sg, r, ip, parts[0] + '/' + parts[1] AS section_id` in `read_candidates`, which §6 landed and §8's map stage will consume), `imas_codex/ids/validation.py:842` (`section = "/".join(parts[:2]) if len(parts) >= 2 else ids_name`, an independent re-derivation of the same rule), and `imas_codex/ids/assembler.py:187` (`m.target_id.startswith(f"{self.ids_name}/{section_name}")`, an independent containment test — exactly what §8's new guard restates). The owner to extend is `read_candidates` in `imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py`, which already returns the section on every edge; a shared `section_of(path)` / `in_section(target, section)` helper beside it would let validation.py:842 and assembler.py:187 drop their copies and let §8's guard be a call rather than a fourth statement.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §8 extends existing deep modules rather than adding a module: the candidate/edge state stays behind `graph_ops` (`write_candidates`/`read_candidates`/`select_candidates`/`clear_candidates`/`write_mapping_binding`/`clear_mapping_bindings`), retrieval and judgment stay behind `ids/candidates.py`, and the map stage's `TargetAssignment` construction stays in `ids/mapping.py`; no spread of shallow wrappers is proposed.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the "section = IDS top-level ancestor" derivation and its containment test already have two owners in the tree and §8 adds a third consumer without naming them.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — this week's counts are public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §8 states what it adds (`read_candidates`, `select_candidates`) and what it retires (`count_sources_by_mapping_status`, the `workers.py` copy of `count_candidates_by_route`, the `--skip-metadata`/`--skip-errors` options, three `mapping_target_*` fields), and the two remaining nodes add none to any of the four families, so the section accounts for its surface.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the mechanisms it extends and reuses each one: `imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py` (the candidate/edge owner), `discovery/base/claims.py` (`claim_batch`, verified present at claims.py:255 and used by `claim_sources_for_candidates`), `assembler.adiscover_assembly` and `_prepare_section_context` (mapping.py:1142, still the map prompt's context builder), `read_candidates`/`select_candidates` (graph_ops.py:576/:636) and `fetch_cross_facility_mappings`; §8 adds no new subsystem.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the only new public functions §8 introduces are `read_candidates` and `select_candidates`, and the plan states in its own text why the second cannot be folded into the writer (`write_candidates` deletes and rewrites every edge, while a pick must flag existing edges without disturbing the shortlist), which is the justification the item asks for.
